The imaging features strongly corroborate this, specifically the presence of a significant necrotic core ('NCR Volume (mL)' of 7.411) and 'Marked' 'Enhancement Quality' with a 'Thickness of enhancing margin' >3mm. These are classic radiological hallmarks of glioblastoma. one_p_nineteen_q.reasoning: This prediction is performed independently of the IDH status prediction. The presence of marked, thick-rimmed enhancement ('Enhancement Quality': 'Marked', 'Thickness of enhancing margin': '>3mm') and a large necrotic component ('NCR Volume (mL)': 7.411) are highly characteristic of an astrocytic lineage tumor (either IDH-mutant astrocytoma or IDH-wildtype glioblastoma), which are by definition 1p/19q non-codeleted. Conversely, these features are highly atypical for oligodendroglioma (which is defined by 1p/19q co-deletion), as these tumors typically show less aggressive features. There are no imaging features in the provided data to suggest a co-deleted status.

Necrosis is a defining feature of WHO Grade 4 gliomas. This is further supported by other features of high-grade biology, including 'Marked' 'Enhancement Quality' and a thick enhancing margin. The patient's advanced age ('age_years': 80) also significantly increases the pre-test probability of a Grade 4 tumor. There is no substantial evidence to support a lower grade diagnosis.
